analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md (head 1-4) and docs/architecture/inference.md (head 810-813, 829, 1896-1899). They describe two behavior changes whose Swift source is not in this batch.

(1) The GLM5NextProcessor now indexes variable-frame-rate (VFR) video frames in presentation order. Frame i is timed at i/nominalFrameRate instead of the clip being refused with 400. The docs say the decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes 512 MiB), the 2 FPS sampler, the 28,532 visual-token cap and maxVideoDurationSeconds 600 are unchanged.

(2) MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders newly accepts the labels data:video/mov and data:video/x-m4v. The docs say MemoryBackedVideoAsset still sniffs MP4/QuickTime from the bytes, so the label only gates the part.

Relevant threats: T-050 (inline video plaintext/temporary files), TB-007 decoder attack surface, ADV-002 malicious consumer DoS, and T-041. For T-041, the docs say media remain excluded from prefix capture (head ~830, CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint), so there is no cache change.

No regression can be established from the docs alone. Integration should verify these points in the GLM5NextProcessor and MediaIngest source:
- A crafted VFR track with a tiny or zero nominalFrameRate cannot produce a division by zero or NaN, an unbounded frame index, or an inflated synthetic duration. For example, many frames at a low average rate could bypass the 600 s duration or frame-count limits, or cause decoding of every frame up to the last sampled one beyond time or memory bounds.
- Sampled-frame count stays bounded by the token ceiling before decode.
- Presentation-order sorting does not allocate unbounded memory for a sample table.
- The new labels still route through the same byte sniffing and the in-memory (non-temp-file) decode path per T-050.
- Nemotron's label set (base lines 95-97) is truly unaffected.
